rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an external device keeps sending its status while a preparation activity runs in parallel with other work, and a later step may only start once the status shows the device is ready: Model the preparation as a task that runs in parallel with the other work. Model each arriving status as a message intermediate catch event that waits for the message, followed by an exclusive gateway that checks readiness. Give the not-ready branch a sequence flow back to the status wait, and give the ready branch a sequence flow to the synchronization point of the parallel work. Do not place the status check after the parallel join, and do not model the repeated status as a single one-time wait.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an external device keeps sending its status while a preparation activity runs in parallel with other work, and a later step may only start once the status shows the device is ready

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a yes/no check on a condition (for example, whether a supply or a state is already in place) and the activities that follow that check are then started together, so the check decides whether the concurrent start is reached: Model an exclusive gateway directly after the activity that establishes the condition, with one labeled flow for each answer. Route the branch that needs a preparatory step through that step and into a separate exclusive merge placed before the parallel gateway that starts the concurrent activities. Do not connect the check straight to the parallel gateway, and do not leave the decision implicit before the concurrent start.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a yes/no check on a condition (for example, whether a supply or a state is already in place) and the activities that follow that check are then started together, so the check decides whether the concurrent start is reached

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description gives two alternative branches (if ... otherwise ...) that both lead to the same next activity, and one branch may include an extra optional step before reaching that activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that alternative paths, chosen by a condition and one of which contains an extra action, come together again so that one following step is performed after either path: Place an exclusive gateway as a merge where the alternative paths meet, before the shared following step. Route each alternative path into that merge gateway, then connect the merge gateway to the shared step. Do not route several alternative paths directly into the shared step without a merge gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that alternative paths, chosen by a condition and one of which contains an extra action, come together again so that one following step is performed after either path

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a yes/no condition on the state of something and then gives the opposite case as its own separate sentence (for example 'If X, do A' followed by 'If not X, do B'), with the condition possibly followed by a further check on a different criterion: Model the condition as an exclusive gateway split with one labeled outgoing branch for each stated case, including the opposite case described in the separate sentence, and make the branch for the opposite case perform its stated action. If a further check on a different criterion follows one of the cases, place a second exclusive gateway on that branch. Rejoin alternative branches that reach a common later element with an exclusive merge placed just before it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a yes/no condition on the state of something and then gives the opposite case as its own separate sentence (for example 'If X, do A' followed by 'If not X, do B'), with the condition possibly followed by a further check on a different criterion

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an activity may optionally be carried out (for example 'may also conduct' an activity), with no condition beyond the team's own choice, and the process continues with a shared step afterwards: Model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway split, with a labeled bypass flow that skips it. Connect the end of the optional activity and the bypass flow into a separate exclusive gateway merge placed before the shared step. Do not link the optional activity directly to the following step, and do not omit the split or the merge.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a conditional check (for example 'if you have it in stock, check how much is left; if it is under a stated amount, add it to the list') where the conditioned step is performed only when the condition holds, and the process continues afterwards regardless of the outcome
